messages:
maria: heads up — saw prefix cache hit-rate drop ~14% on the RAG long-context workload after yesterday's kernel selector change. breaking down by route looks like chat-rag paths worst affected.
ajay: is this the int8 kernel swap? saw a few perf diffs in canary but not that large.
maria: yep, int8-optimized kernels got promoted for A100 pools. perf-bot alerted at 03:12 with reg fingerprint.
perf-bot: [ALERT] prefix_cache_hit_rate drop on customer-prod/rag-service — baseline 72.8% -> 58.3% over last 2h. investigation ticket #INF-4829
sam: quick numbers from prod traces: completions routes stable (~74%), chat-with-prefix down to 55%, structured-output endpoints 49%. looks correlated with longer convo prefixes and multi-role messages.
natalie: could be cache key normalization. we changed hash key concat order in runtime v3.2.2 to reduce collisions: used "sha1(role + '|' + prefix)" instead of old "sha1(prefix + '|' + role)" — might be incompatible with older prefix fingerprints stored on disk.
ajay: ugh, that ordering change wasn't supposed to affect existing cache entries. But we also changed trimming behaviour for trailing spaces in prefix normalization.
maria: reproducer locally: load old cache dump, run new runtime -> miss for identical logical prefix.

sam: quick snippet from repro:
```
# old key
key_old = sha1(prefix + '|' + role)
# new key
key_new = sha1(role + '|' + prefix)
assert key_old == key_new  # FAIL
```

maria: interestingly, shorter prompts still hit. it's the long contexts (>= 1024 tokens) that fall out — probably because of fragmentation + trimming differences.
ajay: Also saw a subtle kernel-related serialization change: the new kernel path does KVCache segmenting per-blob, which changes on-disk prefix chunk boundaries. If keying uses chunk offsets, that could break reuse.
natalie: action items: 1) add compatibility layer to accept both old/new key formats when lookup fails, 2) patch normalizer to canonicalize whitespace exactly as legacy, 3) run canary for chat-rag heavy workloads.
maria: I'll prototype compatibility lookup (try both key variants) and shadow-read hits to metrics. target a patch + canary today.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for artifactory:runtime-v3.2.3-compat at pool-a (5 hosts)
ajay: for warmup strategies we should try proactive prefix-prefetch for RAG queries — we can prefetch top-k prefixes from DB when a new convo opens. cheap async warmup.
sam: also propose a batching heuristic tweak: when prefix hit-rate low, prefer smaller batches to avoid increasing tail latency while waiting for cache fetches.
maria: good point. current batcher coalesces up to 64 requests; for routes with <60% cache hit maybe clamp to 16.
natalie: logging: add a per-request tag `cache_key_variant` with values [legacy, canonical, both_attempted] so we can measure adoption and hit balance over next 48h.

maria: patch uploaded: https://redwood.internal/patches/INF-4829/1 — implements dual-key lookup + whitespace canonicalizer.
ajay: run loadtest: rag-sim 10k qps for 15m against canary pool.
perf-bot: loadtest result: canary hit-rate improved from 58% -> 71% on rag-sim, latency p95 back to baseline. no kernel fallback events.

sam: looks promising. we should still roll a reversible migration: keep dual-lookup for 7 days then flip to canonical-only after metrics stable.
maria: agree. I'll also add a small script to backfill hot prefixes into the new canonical keys for the Dedicated caches.

natalie: owners: @maria (compat patch + backfill), @ajay (batcher clamp experiment), @sam (load tests + rollout plan). I'll open the migration PR and add rollout playbook.
maria: thanks — will monitor alerts and post updates.
ajay: one more note — kernel selector team: consider exposing a flag to avoid changing on-disk serialization semantics during kernel experiments. small compatibility guard would prevent this class of regression.
maria: noted, I'll loop in @kernel-team in #eng-runtime later today.

deploy-bot: canary successful on pool-a, promoting to pool-b (20 hosts)
perf-bot: [OK] prefix_cache_hit_rate recovered for affected routes. closing alert if stable for 1h. :thumbsup:
maria: closing once 1h stable. great cross-team response, nice debugging everyone.
